Publications and Research Outputs

Papers Submitted for Peer Review

Trade Hubs and the Uneven Gains from Globalization: Urban and Rural Disparities from Satellite Nighttime Lights Data

with Hisahiro Naito

This study examines whether the gains from export-driven globalization are distributed evenly across regions. Using satellite-measured nighttime luminosity across developing countries, the research shows that trade-related growth is concentrated in urban trade hubs relative to surrounding rural areas, highlighting the importance of spatially inclusive trade policies.

The Effect of Exchange Rate Volatility and Labor Market Rigidity on Export Growth

with Hisahiro Naito

This paper investigates how exchange rate uncertainty interacts with labor market rigidity to influence export performance using country–industry panel data. The study contributes to understanding how macroeconomic uncertainty and labor market institutions jointly shape international competitiveness.

Can DMSP Night Light Capture Household-Level Welfare? Evidence from a Cluster-Level Quasi-Panel of the Demographic and Health Survey

with Hisahiro Naito

This study evaluates whether satellite nighttime luminosity can serve as a proxy for household welfare in countries where conventional survey data are limited. It explores the potential of remote sensing indicators for monitoring socioeconomic development.

Differential Farming Systems, Farm Productivity, and Resource Use Efficiency: The Case of Wheat Production in Afghanistan

with Mohammad Abdul Malek and Kenichi Kashiwagi

This research applies an endogeneity-corrected stochastic frontier model to household-level agricultural survey data to analyze productivity differences and resource-use efficiency among wheat-producing households in Afghanistan.

Working Papers

The Interaction Effect of Unpredictable Exchange Rate Shocks and Labor Market Rigidity on Export Growth: An Analysis Based on Country–Industry Data

with Hisahiro Naito

This study examines how unpredictable exchange rate shocks interact with labor market rigidity to affect export growth.

Work in Progress

The Effects of Exports on Infant Mortality: A Panel Data Analysis of Sub-Saharan African Countries

with Hisahiro Naito

Examines the relationship between export expansion and child health outcomes across Sub-Saharan African countries.

The Effects of Trade on Child Labor in Sub-Saharan Africa: Evidence Using a Trade-Cost Instrument

Investigates the effects of trade integration on child labor using a trade-cost-based identification strategy.

The Effects of Landlockedness on Trade, Market Access and Household Welfare: Evidence from Ethiopia’s Loss of Sea Access as a Natural Experiment

Studies how changes in trade connectivity and transportation costs affect market access and household welfare.
